If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for pessimism.  
If sentiment shifts from positive to negative over last 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day for mid horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is mixed (±0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to counteract sentiment-induced underestimation.  
If sentiment is uniformly negative over last 7 days and forecast is above 65, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to align with bearish sentiment dominance.
